test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of these was NOT a cause of popular resentment against British rule before 1857?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Religious tolerance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Religious tolerance** was not a cause of resentment against British rule before 1857.
 
• The British did not impose any strict policies targeting religious practices or belief systems of Indians during this period.
 
• While there were cultural and religious tensions, this was not due to the British promoting **religious tolerance**, but rather their interference in certain practices like the abolition of **Sati** and introduction of reforms such as the **Widow Remarriage Act**.
 
• In fact, some Indians saw the British as interfering in their religious practices rather than promoting tolerance.
 
• The resentment before 1857 was primarily fueled by economic, social, and racial factors, rather than religious tolerance.
 
• Key causes of resentment included **economic exploitation**, **land revenue policies**, and the perception of British racial superiority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Low wages**__

 __
 
• Low wages were a significant reason for dissatisfaction among Indian workers and soldiers employed under British rule.
 
• Indian soldiers in the British army were paid much less compared to their British counterparts, which led to **economic disparity** and discontent.
 
• The exploitation of Indian labor in factories, plantations, and administrative roles also contributed to resentment.
 
 
 
• **High taxes**__
 __
 
• **High taxes** were a major grievance against British rule before 1857.
 
• The British introduced exploitative land revenue systems like the **Permanent Settlement**, which forced farmers to pay high taxes irrespective of their agricultural yield.
 
• This led to widespread poverty, famine, and dispossession among Indian peasants.
 
 
 
• **Racial discrimination**__
 
 
• **Racial discrimination** was rampant under British rule and a major cause of resentment.
 
• Indians were treated as inferior to Europeans, both socially and politically.
 
• Indians were excluded from higher administrative positions and faced systemic discrimination in various spheres of life.
